description: Return the factorial of n (n!). Assume n >= 0.
test:
assert factorial(0) == 1
assert factorial(1) == 1
assert factorial(5) == 120
assert factorial(7) == 5040
print('PASS')

description: Return True if string s is a palindrome, False otherwise
test:
assert is_palindrome('racecar') == True
assert is_palindrome('hello') == False
assert is_palindrome('a') == True
assert is_palindrome('abba') == True
print('PASS')

description: Return the sum of all numbers in the list
test:
assert sum_list([1, 2, 3]) == 6
assert sum_list([]) == 0
assert sum_list([-1, 1]) == 0
assert sum_list([10, 20, 30]) == 60
print('PASS')

description: Return how many times x appears in lst
test:
assert count_occurrences([1, 2, 2, 3], 2) == 2
assert count_occurrences([], 5) == 0
assert count_occurrences([7, 7, 7], 7) == 3
assert count_occurrences([1, 2, 3], 9) == 0
print('PASS')

description: Return 'Fizz' if n divisible by 3, 'Buzz' if by 5, 'FizzBuzz' if both, else return n as string
test:
assert fizzbuzz(3) == 'Fizz'
assert fizzbuzz(5) == 'Buzz'
assert fizzbuzz(15) == 'FizzBuzz'
assert fizzbuzz(7) == '7'
print('PASS')

description: Return a new list with duplicates removed, preserving original order
test:
assert remove_duplicates([1, 2, 2, 3]) == [1, 2, 3]
assert remove_duplicates([]) == []
assert remove_duplicates([5, 5, 5]) == [5]
assert remove_duplicates([1, 2, 3]) == [1, 2, 3]
print('PASS')

description: Convert Celsius temperature to Fahrenheit
test:
assert celsius_to_fahrenheit(0) == 32.0
assert celsius_to_fahrenheit(100) == 212.0
assert celsius_to_fahrenheit(-40) == -40.0
assert celsius_to_fahrenheit(37) == 98.6
print('PASS')

description: Return the number of words in string s (words are separated by spaces)
test:
assert count_words('hello world') == 2
assert count_words('') == 0
assert count_words('one') == 1
assert count_words('a b c d') == 4
print('PASS')

description: Flatten a one-level nested list into a single list
test:
assert flatten([[1, 2], [3, 4]]) == [1, 2, 3, 4]
assert flatten([[], [1], [2, 3]]) == [1, 2, 3]
assert flatten([[5]]) == [5]
assert flatten([]) == []
print('PASS')

description: Return True if n is a prime number, False otherwise. Assume n >= 2.
test:
assert is_prime(2) == True
assert is_prime(3) == True
assert is_prime(4) == False
assert is_prime(17) == True
assert is_prime(18) == False
print('PASS')

description: Return the second largest number in the list. Assume list has at least 2 distinct values.
test:
assert second_largest([1, 2, 3]) == 2
assert second_largest([5, 1, 4, 2]) == 4
assert second_largest([10, 10, 9]) == 9
assert second_largest([3, 1]) == 1
print('PASS')

description: Return the string with the first letter of every word capitalized
test:
assert capitalize_words('hello world') == 'Hello World'
assert capitalize_words('python is fun') == 'Python Is Fun'
assert capitalize_words('a') == 'A'
assert capitalize_words('already Done') == 'Already Done'
print('PASS')

description: Return the average (mean) of a list of numbers. Assume the list is non-empty.
test:
assert list_average([1, 2, 3]) == 2.0
assert list_average([10]) == 10.0
assert list_average([0, 0, 0]) == 0.0
assert list_average([1, 3]) == 2.0
print('PASS')

description: Merge two sorted lists into one sorted list
test:
assert merge_sorted([1, 3, 5], [2, 4, 6]) == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
assert merge_sorted([], [1, 2]) == [1, 2]
assert merge_sorted([1], []) == [1]
assert merge_sorted([1, 2], [1, 2]) == [1, 1, 2, 2]
print('PASS')

description: Return True if s1 and s2 are anagrams of each other, False otherwise
test:
assert is_anagram('listen', 'silent') == True
assert is_anagram('hello', 'world') == False
assert is_anagram('abc', 'cab') == True
assert is_anagram('abc', 'ab') == False
print('PASS')

description: Return value clamped between lo and hi inclusive
test:
assert clamp(5, 1, 10) == 5
assert clamp(-3, 0, 10) == 0
assert clamp(15, 0, 10) == 10
assert clamp(0, 0, 0) == 0
print('PASS')

description: Return a dict mapping each character in s to its frequency
Given a list of integers from 1 to n with one missing, return the missing number
test:
assert find_missing([1, 2, 4, 5]) == 3
assert find_missing([2, 3, 4, 5]) == 1
assert find_missing([1, 2, 3, 4]) == 5
assert find_missing([1, 3]) == 2
print('PASS')

description: Rotate list to the right by k positions
test:
assert rotate_list([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 2) == [4, 5, 1, 2, 3]
assert rotate_list([1, 2, 3], 0) == [1, 2, 3]
assert rotate_list([1], 5) == [1]
assert rotate_list([1, 2, 3], 3) == [1, 2, 3]
print('PASS')

description: Return the longest word in the string s. If tie, return the first one.
test:
assert longest_word('I love programming') == 'programming'
assert longest_word('hi') == 'hi'
assert longest_word('cat bat sat') == 'cat'
assert longest_word('short longer longest') == 'longest'
print('PASS')
